About Us

The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we are committed to continually improving our healthcare system. The Department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity

As the Director of Accountability and Analytics
, you will have an opportunity to influence how physician services are planned, funded, monitored and improved across Nova Scotia’s health system.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will be a key member of the leadership team advancing strategic priorities across the physician services portfolio. Your leadership will span two connected areas: strengthening accountability for physician remuneration and funded programs, including support for major negotiations, and building the branch’s data and analytics capability to enable stronger, evidence-informed decisions.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader who is comfortable working at the intersection of policy, funding, accountability, analytics and health-system transformation
. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, work with senior partners across government and the health system, and translate complex financial, operational, policy and analytical information into practical frameworks, meaningful insights and clear advice.

Your work will help strengthen performance and accountability while building the data and analytical capabilities needed to support the future of physician services in Nova Scotia.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you will provide strategic leadership to complex initiatives that strengthen accountability and expand the use of data in physician services planning, funding and performance management.

You will lead multidisciplinary teams, establish priorities and create the conditions for high-quality, decision-focused work. Working across the Department, government, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health and external organizations, you will bring partners together to move initiatives from design through implementation, measurement and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities Include

Strengthening accountability by designing and improving frameworks, performance measures and monitoring approaches for physician remuneration models and funded initiatives.
Leading complex initiatives that establish clear outcomes, roles, decision-making responsibilities, reporting requirements and approaches to managing risk.
Supporting major negotiations through scenario analysis, costing, evidence synthesis, mandate development and recommendations related to Physician Agreement and Clinical/Academic Funding Plan negotiations.
Building analytics capability by advancing a branch data and analytics strategy focused on data quality, governance, access and integration, including the transition to modern cloud-based platforms.
Turning data into insight by overseeing dashboards, Power BI reporting, forecasting tools and provincial measures related to financial performance, service delivery, access, health human resources and outcomes.
Ensuring analytical integrity through appropriate methods, controls and documentation that support reliable and well-governed analysis.
Leading and developing people while building capability in project delivery, accountability, business intelligence and advanced analytics.
Building trusted partnerships and collaborative approaches to complex issues where perspectives and priorities may differ.
Influencing decisions by translating complex information into clear briefings, presentations and recommendations for senior audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a strategic and collaborative leader who can bring clarity to complex issues and turn evidence into action. You are comfortable working with senior leaders and system partners, guiding multidisciplinary teams, and translating complex analytical, financial, operational and policy information into clear advice.

You have a Bachelor’s Degree
in a relevant field such as public or business administration, health administration, data or health analytics, economics, finance, engineering, computer science or a related discipline, plus significant years of progressively responsible experience
. This includes at least three years in a leadership or management role
involving complex projects, organizational change, accountability, performance measurement or data-informed decision-making in the public, health or a similarly complex sector. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

You Bring Demonstrated Experience In

Leading and developing professional or multidisciplinary teams.
Leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from design through implementation, measurement and continuous improvement.
Building or strengthening organizational, accountability or analytical capabilities.
Designing accountability frameworks, performance measures or evaluation approaches.
Translating complex data, policy, financial and operational information into clear advice for senior decision-makers.
Building productive relationships with senior partners where perspectives, priorities or implementation considerations may differ.

Experience supporting complex negotiations, health-system funding or physician remuneration is considered an asset. A Master’s Degree in a complementary discipline is also an asset.

Experience with modern data and business intelligence platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Azure, Power BI or comparable technologies
is an asset. Hands-on technical development experience is not required; however, you must be able to lead technical specialists, assess analytical approaches and ensure data products align with business and policy needs.

We may assess qualifications and competencies through tools such as scenario-based exercises, standardized assessments, presentations, interviews and reference checks.

Equivalency

An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions

Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day.
May be required to work overtime on occasion.

What We Offer

Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Job Description

The Director, Capital Investment & Decision Support will lead and grow AMCL’s Capital Investment & Decision Support capability, working with asset-intensive organizations to improve how they plan, prioritize and make investment decisions across the asset lifecycle.

The role will combine senior client advisory, technical leadership, business development and team leadership. It will support clients across Infrastructure and Energy & Natural Resources to establish practical, evidence-based approaches to asset investment planning, lifecycle decision-making, risk, value and portfolio prioritization.

The Director will work closely with AMCL and Turner & Townsend colleagues across asset management, program and project delivery, controls, cost and commercial management, digital and data, bringing these capabilities together where clients require integrated solution

Key Responsibilities

Lead complex client engagements focused on asset investment planning, lifecycle planning, capital prioritization, value-based decision-making and portfolio optimization.
Advise senior client leaders on investment strategy, asset risk, lifecycle performance, affordability and long-term capital requirements.
Develop and apply decision-support frameworks that bring together cost, risk, performance, value and service outcomes to support transparent and defensible investment decisions.
Lead the development of asset investment strategies, long-term capital and renewal plans, prioritization frameworks, value frameworks, business cases and investment governance.
Support clients in developing approaches to asset criticality, risk-informed investment, asset health, lifecycle intervention planning and whole-life cost analysis.
Lead the development and application of multi-criteria decision analysis, value-based decision-making, scenario analysis and other structured approaches to investment prioritization.
Help clients establish governance, decision rights, processes and controls for capital planning and asset investment decision-making.
Work with asset information, digital and analytics specialists to improve the quality and use of asset, risk, cost and performance information in investment decisions.
Provide senior technical leadership and quality assurance across AMCL Capital Investment & Decision Support assignments.
Develop AMCL propositions, methods, tools and intellectual property within Capital Investment & Decision Support, drawing on global AMCL experience and relevant industry practice.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders and identify opportunities to extend AMCL’s support where there is a clear client need.
Lead and contribute to proposals, pursuits, presentations and commercial development activity.
Work with AMCL and Turner & Townsend sector and service-line leaders to develop opportunities across Infrastructure and Energy & Natural Resources.
Lead, coach and develop consultants working across asset investment planning, lifecycle management, risk, value and decision support.

Description

ProgressionLIVE développe des logiciels web et mobiles de gestion des opérations de service sur le terrain, utilisés par des centaines d’organisations canadiennes dans les secteurs du CVC, de la plomberie, de l’électricité, de la construction, du transport et de la maintenance.

Votre rôle

Relevant du directeur général, vous dirigerez toute l’équipe produit et technologie et serez responsable de la feuille de route et de la livraison. Vous définirez avec le directeur général les orientations produit, les priorités majeures et les investissements structurants, tout en exerçant votre autonomie sur les décisions courantes et l’exécution.

Vous combinerez jugement produit, leadership et contribution technique directe : accompagner les développeurs, renforcer leurs compétences avec l’IA et programmer certaines fonctionnalités jusqu’à leur mise en production. Vous vous appuierez sur les expertises de l’équipe pour les décisions techniques spécialisées.

Vos responsabilités

Piloter la feuille de route à partir des échanges clients, des données d’utilisation et des objectifs commerciaux. Collaborer avec les ventes et le service client, puis mesurer l’adoption et l’impact.
Diriger l’exécution : définir la portée, organiser les priorités, lever les obstacles et accompagner l’équipe jusqu’à la mise en production et à la validation des résultats.
Programmer et livrer certaines fonctionnalités, en respectant les exigences de tests, de revue de code et de sécurité. Créer aussi des prototypes et des outils internes.
Recruter et développer l’équipe. Accompagner les développeurs par le travail en binôme, les revues de code, la formation et le partage des connaissances.
Définir et diriger un modèle opérationnel activé par l’IA pour le produit et l’ingénierie. Habiliter les développeurs, l’assurance qualité et les DevOps à utiliser l’IA efficacement tout au long du cycle de vie du développement, de la recherche et des spécifications à la mise en œuvre, aux tests, à l’examen du code, à la documentation, au débogage, au déploiement et à la réponse aux incidents.
Identifier et automatiser les activités répétitives ou à faible valeur ajoutée. Prototyper les flux de travail agentic à fort impact et les outils internes, les évaluer en fonction des améliorations mesurables dans la vitesse de livraison, la qualité, la fiabilité et la capacité de l’équipe, pas seulement les taux d’adoption.
Établir des normes pratiques pour l’utilisation responsable de l’IA (sécurité, confidentialité, propriété intellectuelle, qualité, responsabilité). Créer une culture d’expérimentation tout en veillant à ce que les gens restent responsables de l’exactitude et de la sécurité.
Identifier les opportunités d’IA orientées client qui créent une valeur significative et différenciée, distinguant les capacités authentiques des features motivées par la nouveauté. Partenaire avec les clients et l’équipe pour valider et hiérarchiser.
Équilibrer nouvelles fonctionnalités, dette technique, fiabilité et sécurité. Évaluer les compromis avec l’équipe et maintenir des exigences claires de qualité et de confidentialité.

Votre profil

8+ années de leadership en développement logiciel, incluant la construction et la mise à l’échelle d’équipes d’ingénierie.
Expérience pratique en développement logiciel et capacité actuelle à comprendre une base de code, programmer, tester et livrer des fonctionnalités en production.
Expérience de direction d’une équipe de développement, avec responsabilité de la livraison et capacité à recruter, coacher et faire progresser les développeurs.
Solide jugement produit : comprendre les problèmes clients, piloter une feuille de route, prioriser les investissements et mesurer les résultats.
Maîtrise pratique des outils de développement assisté par l’IA et capacité à transmettre des méthodes efficaces, avec validation critique du code généré.
Bonne maîtrise du français et de l’anglais pour collaborer avec les équipes et utiliser la documentation technique.

Notre environnement technologique

Java, Spring, Hibernate, Vue 3, TypeScript, AWS, GitHub Actions et Terraform. Nos applications mobiles fonctionnent hors ligne et se synchronisent. La maîtrise de chaque technologie n’est pas requise.

jobs.description:
Senior Regional Vice President

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Senior Regional Vice President (SRVP) is responsible for leading and managing overall business operations, market development, strategic execution, and organizational management within a designated region, ensuring that regional operational goals align with the company’s overarching strategic direction. This role entails comprehensive oversight of regional business performance, operational management, financial results, market expansion, client relations, and team development. The SRVP drives sustainable growth within the region while ensuring that all business activities comply with company policies, standards, and management requirements.

The SRVP works closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, other regional leaders, and the corporate executive team to formulate regional development strategies, facilitate cross-regional resource coordination, oversee the execution of major business initiatives, and resolve critical operational issues. Furthermore, the SRVP is responsible for cultivating regional management talent, optimizing operational systems, and enhancing market competitiveness to ensure long-term, stable business growth and operational success within the assigned region.

Key Responsibilities

I. Regional Strategic Planning and Leadership

Develop and implement long-term development strategies and annual operational plans for the assigned region, ensuring that regional objectives are aligned with the company’s overall strategy, financial goals, and market development direction. Analyze the regional market environment, industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer needs to identify new business opportunities and potential risks. Establish regional management standards and execution mechanisms, define the responsibilities, objectives, and performance requirements for each business unit, and drive the effective implementation of regional strategies.

II. Regional Business Operations and Performance Management

Provide comprehensive oversight of the daily operations of all business departments, branches, and operational units within the region, ensuring that business processes run efficiently and meet established performance targets. Regularly review revenue performance, operational efficiency, service quality, customer satisfaction, and business growth; identify operational deviations promptly and develop corrective measures. Coordinate activities across different departments within the region to resolve significant issues that impact business execution and operational efficiency.

III. Financial Management and Operational Goal Control

Oversee regional budget development, financial planning, cost control, and the analysis of operational results, ensuring that regional financial objectives align with the company’s overall financial plan. Collaborate with the CFO and the finance team to review regional revenue, profit, operating expenses, cash flow, and return on investment (ROI). Establish mechanisms for monitoring budget execution and financial performance; control operating costs effectively; enhance the efficiency of regional resource utilization; and ensure that all business units achieve their established financial objectives.

IV. Market Expansion and Business Growth

Lead regional market development, business expansion, and commercial growth initiatives, identifying potential customer segments, emerging markets, and strategic partnership opportunities. Oversee the development of sales channels, customer acquisition, marketing campaigns, and business collaborations to drive the growth of regional market share and enhance corporate brand influence. Partner with business development, sales, and marketing teams to formulate market-entry strategies and customer growth plans, ensuring the sustained competitiveness of the regional business.

V. Organizational Management and Team Leadership

Responsible for establishing and refining the regional management structure, and overseeing the performance of regional department heads and senior management. Define team performance objectives, talent development programs, and succession plans for management roles to strengthen regional organizational capabilities and the execution proficiency of the leadership team. Foster a positive corporate culture and cross-departmental collaboration, ensuring that managers at all levels effectively implement company policies, operational goals, and management requirements.

VI. Customer Relations and Strategic Partnership Management

Oversee the management of key regional customer relationships, strategic partnerships, and major commercial contracts, ensuring timely responses to customer needs and the stability of collaborative ties. Participate in negotiations with major clients, business collaborations, and the drafting and review of critical business agreements; coordinate the resolution of significant customer complaints, service disputes, and partnership-related issues. Collaborate with customer success, sales, and operations teams to improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and long-term partnership value.

VII. Risk Management and Compliance Oversight

Monitor operational, financial, legal, and market risks within regional business activities, and establish effective mechanisms for risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Ensure that all regional business units comply with applicable laws, industry regulations, internal corporate policies, and regulatory requirements. Work with legal, compliance, finance, and internal audit teams to periodically review regional management processes and internal controls, addressing significant compliance issues promptly and driving the implementation of corrective actions.

VIII. Communication with Senior Management and Strategic Execution

Provide regular reports to the CEO, COO, and the corporate executive management team regarding regional operational performance, market developments, financial results, business risks, and the progress of strategic plan execution. Provide management counsel regarding regional expansion, organizational restructuring, major investments, and business transformation. Facilitate the sharing of resources and information between various regions and corporate headquarters, ensure the unified execution of corporate strategy at the regional level, and drive long-term, sustainable growth for regional operations.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Financial Management, Economics, or a related field.

A Master of Business Administration (MBA) or a postgraduate degree in a relevant field is preferred.

Prior training in areas such as corporate operations management, strategic planning, financial management, or leadership is an advantage.

Proficiency in corporate management, regional market strategy, budget management, and risk control principles.

Work Experience

At least 20 years of professional experience in corporate management, business operations, market expansion, or regional management.

At least 7 years of experience in senior management or regional leadership roles.

Proven, hands-on experience in managing multiple business units, branches, or cross-regional operational teams.

A successful track record in developing regional business strategies, managing budgets, driving business growth, and enhancing operational performance.

Experience in managing cross-regional operations, or working within large-scale or multinational corporate environments, is preferred.

AT NDI, THE WORK YOU DO HERE MAKES A DIFFERENCE.

Every day, your work supports the advancement of medical technology.
NDI is the recognized global leader and industry pioneer of Optical and Electromagnetic tracking technology. Backed by decades of innovation and expertise, we’re the strategic partner of choice for the world’s top medical device OEMs, advancing the development of OEM navigation platforms. Leading OEM navigation platforms rely on our technologies for accuracy and reliability across demanding applications, and as a strategic partner, we support them from concept through integration to commercialization.
Whether you're designing technology, supporting customers, or enabling the teams behind them, your work matters. Every role at NDI plays a part in shaping the future of medical technology innovation.

THE IMPACT YOU WILL MAKE:

As NDI’s Vice President, Global Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs, you will shape the quality and regulatory strategy for our global operations and medical and non-medical product portfolio. In this new role, you will bring teams and sites together, strengthen our Quality Management System, and guide regulatory strategies that enable product development, market access, and sustainable growth.

Reporting to the President, you will bring an independent quality and regulatory perspective to executive decisions, helping protect product reliability, customer confidence, and patient safety. You will develop functional and site leaders, establish clear decision-making authority and accountability, and build the capabilities needed for long-term success.

HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE:

Set and execute NDI’s global quality and regulatory strategy, translating business priorities into annual plans, measurable objectives, budgets, and resource investments.
Lead the global QA/RA organization, defining its structure and resource priorities, developing functional and site leaders, and strengthening delegation and leadership succession.
Foster a culture of quality across the organization, partnering with leaders to embed clear ownership of quality and compliance into everyday decisions and operations.
Lead global Quality Management System governance and performance, simplifying and aligning practices across sites while holding leaders accountable for applicable standards, regulatory, and customer requirements.
Shape global regulatory strategy and market access priorities for new and existing products, overseeing submissions, registrations, and lifecycle compliance within NDI’s scope of responsibility.
Develop a strong understanding of NDI’s spatial measurement technologies, customer applications, and supply chain to guide cross-functional quality and regulatory decisions.
Provide executive oversight of design, software, and manufacturing process quality, ensuring appropriate design controls, verification, validation, and risk management throughout the product lifecycle.
Oversee supplier and contract manufacturer quality, product acceptance and release, nonconformances, and corrective and preventive action (CAPA).
Drive measurable improvements in product and process quality through data analysis, effective root-cause investigation, and prevention of recurring issues.
Establish oversight of complaints, post-market monitoring, safety assessments, reporting, and field actions, ensuring timely investigation, escalation, and resolution by accountable leaders.
Provide executive oversight of regulatory inspection and audit readiness, ensuring leaders deliver effective preparation, responses, and sustained corrective action.
Represent NDI in significant regulatory matters and strategic customer and supplier discussions, while empowering functional leaders to manage routine interactions.
Set global performance measures and management review expectations, evaluate results with leaders, and advise the President and executive team on risks, investment needs, and improvement priorities.
Anticipate the business impact of evolving regulations and standards, setting priorities and sponsoring implementation programs that support compliance and business continuity.
Establish clear escalation pathways and decision-making authority, exercising independent judgment on significant quality risks and authorizing or recommending action within delegated authority.

EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, or a related technical discipline; an advanced degree or relevant quality or regulatory certification is an asset.
15+ years of progressive medical device QA and/or regulatory affairs experience, with substantial responsibility across both functions.
7+ years of senior leadership experience, leading managers or functional leaders across multiple sites or international markets.
Experience setting global regulatory strategy and leading quality systems in regulated medical device manufacturing, translating requirements into practical systems that maintain compliance, enable market access, and protect product quality and patient safety.
In-depth knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971 and medical device risk management; FDA requirements, including QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), reporting, corrections and removals, and complaint handling; and regulatory frameworks in Canada, the EU, UK, Switzerland, Japan and South Africa, including Health Canada requirements and EU MDR, as applicable to the product portfolio.
Experience leading regulatory inspections and audits, guiding the resolution of significant quality issues, and overseeing CAPA, supplier quality, and post-market processes.
Experience supporting products from development through manufacturing and commercialization, including design controls, technical documentation and change management.
Experience with electronic quality systems and data-driven improvement; experience leading a quality organization through significant growth or global process alignment is strongly preferred.
Experience with spatial measurement, embedded hardware, software-enabled technology, OEM medical device partnerships or sterile medical device manufacturing is an asset.

ADDITIONAL STRENGTHS:

Executive judgment that balances quality, regulatory, business, customer, and patient safety priorities.
Ability to challenge decisions constructively, communicate risk clearly, and influence senior leaders and technical teams.
Collaborative leadership that builds trust across functions and sites, develops leaders, and enables organizational change.

QA/RA REQUIREMENTS:

jobs.title: Senior Director of Product Management, Endpoint Security and XDR
jobs.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role:

Elastic Security is hiring a Senior Director of Product Management to lead our Endpoint Security & XDR business. This role reports to the GM of Elastic Security. You will be paired with our most senior engineering leader, a VP who leads all of Elastic Security engineering and whose day-to-day focus is endpoint, sharing accountability for the line's outcomes with you. You will also peer with the product lead of our SIEM and analytics business as we build one platform together. The endpoint is where we meet the adversary directly, and where the people we serve, the analysts and defenders protecting hospitals, banks, and government networks, need us most. Their mission is our mission, and this role carries that responsibility for the endpoint and XDR market. Like Elastic itself, the role is distributed by design.

This business was born when Elastic acquired Endgame in 2019, a pioneer in endpoint prevention, detection, and response with roots in defending national security networks. We extended that protection philosophy to Linux and cloud-native environments with the Cmd acquisition in 2021. The result today is Elastic Defend, and its record in independent testing reflects the quality of the work: Elastic Security was the only vendor to score 100% protection in both the AV-Comparatives Real-World and Malware Protection Tests for all of 2025, and the only vendor among 16 to earn a perfect malware protection score in the 2026 Business Security Test, with zero false alarms on the software businesses actually run. And unlike most of this market, we do that work in the open: our protection artifacts and detection rules are public for anyone to inspect.

This role is open for a straightforward reason. Our product leader is retiring, and we are organizing product management around our two core businesses: SIEM and analytics, which will be led by a proven leader already at Elastic, and endpoint, where we are looking outside for someone who brings a fresh perspective from this market. The timing is deliberate in another way as well: security operations are shifting toward agentic workflows, and as a challenger in this market we can move faster than the incumbents. Our focus with this role is business expertise: we are looking for a business owner who understands endpoint security deeply and who will grow this line with the care of someone who owns the outcome. You will have genuine room to lead. The strategy, the priorities, and how we compete are yours to shape with your engineering partner.

What You Will Be Doing:

Drive the business-driven OKRs for the Endpoint Security & XDR line: revenue contribution, competitive win rate, platform attach, retention, and expansion.
Set the product strategy for the line and represent it with sales leadership, customers, and analysts: a clear diagnosis of the market, a guiding policy, and coherent actions that follow from it.
Own the agentic detection and response strategy for the endpoint: where AI-driven and autonomous capabilities genuinely help prevention, detection, and response at the edge, working closely with the SIEM and analytics line so customers experience one agentic platform, not two roadmaps.
Shape where we invest and where we choose not to, building the case with data and customer evidence.
Own how endpoint and XDR fit the broader Elastic Security platform story, so a customer who lands with endpoint expands into the platform and a SIEM customer sees why our endpoint belongs next to it.
Put customers first. Visit them where they are, participate in deals and win/loss reviews, enable the field, and represent Elastic at tradeshows and industry events. This work requires regular travel.
Partner with your engineering counterpart as a true pair, sharing one set of outcomes for the line.
Lead and develop a team of product managers, helping each of them connect their work to the customer's mission and the business.

What You Bring:

Genuine care for the people this product protects. Customers can tell whether the person across the table is invested in their mission, and this business runs on the trust you earn by caring consistently over time.
Business expertise running a product line or business unit in security, with comfort in the full picture: revenue, win rates, retention, pricing and packaging, and competitive positioning.
Earned credibility in endpoint security: EPP, EDR, XDR, and enough understanding of what an agent does on a machine to have real conversations with engineers and practitioners.
A strong working partnership with go-to-market teams, including experience enabling sellers and supporting deals alongside the field.
A habit of deciding with evidence: win/loss data, customer conversations, and market signals inform your calls.
A point of view on how a challenger competes and differentiates against well-funded incumbents.
Clear executive communication with executive leadership, CISOs, sales leadership, and industry analysts.

Bonus Points:

Experience competing with or working at endpoint-focused security vendors, with perspective on the strengths and gaps across the market.
Experience helping a security business scale from a few hundred million toward $1B.
Familiarity with public efficacy testing (AV-Comparatives, MITRE ATT&CK evaluations) and how to participate in the open.
Experience serving customers in hard environments: regulated industries, classified networks, air-gapped and OT deployments.
A thoughtful position on AI and agentic capabilities at the endpoint, with healthy skepticism of silver bullets and a clear sense of where they genuinely help the defender.
Contributions to open source or the security community. Our work is public, and we value people who build in the open.

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.

Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement

Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

The CFO will maintain a meaningful on-site presence and build strong relationships across both operating locations. Regular travel between St. Thomas and Glencoe is expected as part of developing a deep understanding of the business and supporting operational excellence.

This is an opportunity to join an organization at a defining moment in its journey. For a finance executive who wants to influence strategy, strengthen operations, develop teams, and help create long-term enterprise value, this role offers both challenge and impact.

serves as the District's Financial Officer and provides strategic leadership for financial stewardship, long-term sustainability, governance, and risk management. Financial Strategy & Governance

Financial Systems & Business Operations

Budgeting & Financial Planning

·       Monitor budget performance, report variances to the CAO and Council, and recommend corrective adjustments and cost-saving measures.
Asset Management & Capital Planning
·       Provide executive oversight of asset management and capital planning programs, and oversee service contracts, leases, and lease renewals for District facilities.
·       Oversee procurement and contract management processes.
·       Evaluate the financial implications of major initiatives, capital projects, and service delivery decisions.
·       Oversee lifecycle funding and capital renewal strategies, including grant seeking with the Grants Coordinator.

Risk Management

·       Lead the enterprise risk management framework, including insurance, claims, and financial risk mitigation.
·       Advise Council and senior leadership on emerging organizational risks and mitigation strategies.
Organizational Leadership
·       Contribute to corporate strategy and organizational effectiveness as a member of the Senior Leadership Team.
·       Lead the Finance Department through the Deputy Director of Finance, championing continuous improvement and service excellence.
·       Foster cross-department collaboration, build relationships with Council, auditors, and partners, and engage the public on budget matters.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

·       Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or Public Administration, or a related discipline.
·       Minimum 8-10 years of progressive public sector finance experience, including significant leadership and 2-3 years in local government, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
·       Demonstrated experience advising senior leaders and elected officials on complex financial matters.
·       Thorough knowledge of PSAS, the Community Charter, the Local Government Act, and municipal finance practices.

Skills & Abilities

·       Strategic thinking, sound judgment, and strong financial stewardship, governance, and risk management.
·       Exceptional leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills, with political and organizational acumen.
·       Ability to present complex financial information to Council and the public, and balance operational needs with long-term sustainability.

The District of Peachland offers a collaborative work environment with opportunities for growth. As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the District’s financial future and the success of our community.

Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter outlining their qualifications and experience. This position will remain open until filled.

!

Join FinDev Canada, Canada's development financial institution! Joining FinDev means being part of a growing, purpose-driven organization where your expertise directly contributes to meaningful, measurable impact around the world.

Mobilize private capital toward climate solutions across emerging markets.
Collaborate across investment, blended finance, impact, risk, legal, and strategy teams.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on climate mobilization opportunities and market trends.
Strengthen FinDev Canada's institutional capabilities and thought leadership in climate mobilisation.

Master's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, International Development, Public Policy, or a related field.
Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in climate finance, infrastructure finance, development finance, investment banking, private capital mobilisation, blended finance, or related fields.
Significant experience originating, structuring, or developing complex investment opportunities and strategic partnerships in emerging and developing markets.
Demonstrated experience leading senior stakeholder relationships across public, private, and multilateral sectors.
Strong understanding of climate finance, sustainable investment, capital mobilisation, and development impact.
Proven track record leading high-performing teams and delivering strategic initiatives.
Experience working across multiple functions and influencing senior stakeholders in complex organizational environments.
Bilingual in both official languages (English and French)

Experience within a Development Finance Institution (DFI), Multilateral Development Bank (MDB), impact investor, climate-focused fund manager, or international financial institution.
Deep network across climate finance, institutional investors, sovereign entities, foundations, and development finance partners.
Experience establishing new business lines, platforms, or strategic initiatives.

Additional language capabilities, particularly Spanish

At ABB
, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

Business Manager - Commercial

__

Before a customer selects an automation partner, they need confidence in the people who will deliver. In this role, you will be the person who brings that confidence to life.

As ABB’s Project Director for mega projects and highly complex automation opportunities, you will engage customers from the earliest stages - often before a formal tender exists. Working alongside Sales, you will turn first-hand execution experience into a compelling delivery approach, helping customers understand how ABB will manage complexity, reduce risk and deliver on its commitments.

Your influence will span opportunity identification, pre-FEED and FEED, tendering, negotiation, award and handover - and, where assigned, project execution. The scope includes major automation and integration opportunities across DCS, SIS, PLC/SCADA, electrical systems, digital solutions and advanced process control.

Global Opportunity – Open to Candidates Worldwide
*

While this job posting may display only a limited number of locations, we welcome applications from qualified candidates globally. If you believe your skills and experience match this role, we encourage you to apply regardless of your current location.

This position does not require relocation
. The selected candidate will be employed and hosted through their current ABB location or the nearest suitable ABB office

Your Responsibilities

Establish customer confidence early. Engage owners, EPCs and licensors as ABB’s execution lead, building trusted relationships with project directors, engineering managers, procurement teams and executive stakeholders.
Make delivery experience a competitive advantage. Present credible reference cases that explain project scope, outcomes, challenges, recovery actions and lessons learned.
Shape an execution strategy that works. Develop contracting and delivery approaches covering MAC/MAV models, integration responsibilities, interfaces, standardization, testing, commissioning and the global/local engineering split.
Own the execution commitments in the proposal. Define realistic execution plans, schedules, project organizations, resource requirements, risk registers, and HSE and quality plans, securing internal commitment before submission.
Bring execution judgment into commercial decisions. Assess and quantify risks and opportunities, support cost estimates, contribute to bid/no-bid decisions, and defend the execution case at tender and risk reviews.
Support negotiations with delivery insight. Help establish achievable schedules, clear scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, payment milestones, change mechanisms, warranties and appropriate risk positions.
Preserve continuity after award. Ensure a structured handover of commitments, assumptions, risks and customer expectations. Where assigned, lead execution as Project Director or remain involved as executive sponsor through critical phases.
Strengthen ABB’s pursuit and delivery capability. Collaborate across Sales, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Legal and Finance; coach teams; and feed execution outcomes into future estimates, reference cases and delivery practices.

Your background

A degree in instrumentation, control, electrical, chemical engineering or an equivalent discipline; an executive or business master’s degree is an advantage.
At least 12 years of industrial automation project delivery experience, including substantial responsibility as Project Manager or Project Director on large, complex projects in oil and gas, chemicals, refining or energy.
Full-lifecycle leadership of at least one extra-large or highly complex automation project, together with direct experience recovering a challenged project.
Demonstrated contribution to winning major pursuits, such as MAC selections, FEED-to-EPC conversions or frame agreements.
Deep understanding of EPC delivery, contracting models, interface management and the dynamics between owners, EPCs and technology vendors.
Working knowledge of DCS, SIS, PLC/SCADA, advanced process control and OT/IT convergence, enabling you to connect execution choices with customers’ operational outcomes.
A recognized project management certification, such as PMP, IPMA Level A/B, or an equivalent ABB certification.
Fluent English and willingness to travel extensively

What Will Help You Succeed

You build trust through first-hand delivery experience, candid advice and confidence with customer executives and EPC leaders. You connect execution decisions with commercial value and unite Sales and delivery teams around realistic, shared commitments.

The impact you will make

Engage customers earlier, strengthen ABB’s execution credibility and help win strategic projects - supported by smooth handovers, protected margins and lessons that improve future pursuits.

This opportunity is open to candidates in multiple countries, with the final work location determined based on the selected candidate. As compensation may vary by location, we are committed to being transparent throughout the hiring process and will share details of the salary range, variable compensation and benefits package with candidates who progress to the first interview stage for a location in the European Union, covered by the EU Pay Transparency Directive.

The final offer will be tailored based on your role location, experience, skills and qualifications, internal market positioning and alignment with ABB internal standards.

Directeur(trice) des opérations

Le poste

Eco DCS, une entreprise du Groupe Adag située à Montréal, fournit des infrastructures complètes d’alimentation électrique et de refroidissement pour les centres de données : génératrices diesel, refroidisseurs (chillers), murs de ventilateurs (fan walls), turbines à gaz, appareillage de commutation moyenne tension (MV switchgear) et unités de contrôle électrique.

Le ou la Directeur(trice) des opérations
est responsable de quatre équipes de bout en bout (Approvisionnement, Qualité fournisseurs, Logistique et transport, Mise en service) et veille à ce que tout défaut soit retracé jusqu’au fournisseur et corrigé de façon permanente. Notre philosophie est simple : « Livré. » Offrir des centres de données fiables dans des délais de réalisation réduits.

Portée du rôle
: Les Opérations sont responsables de l’exécution et de la livraison. L’Ingénierie conserve l’autorité technique quant aux exigences, aux critères FAT et ITP, à la disposition des NCR ainsi qu’à la décision finale de mise en service.

Gestionnaires relevant directement du poste :

Gestionnaire Approvisionnement
Gestionnaire Qualité fournisseurs
Gestionnaire Logistique et transport
Directeur(trice) de la mise en service

Rôle, responsabilités et objectifs

Construire la fonction Opérations

Concevoir, recruter et diriger les quatre équipes Opérations, incluant les agents d’approvisionnement, les gestionnaires de la qualité de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, les coordonnateurs logistiques et l’équipe de mise en service.
Collaborer avec les équipes de programme afin d’assurer que l’exécution des projets respecte les meilleures pratiques et les standards de référence.
Rédiger et faire appliquer les procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP) pour l’approvisionnement, le suivi des commandes, l’expédition, la réception, l’inspection et la mise en service.
Mettre en place des outils permettant le suivi des commandes, des expéditions, des non-conformités (NCR) et de l’état d’avancement de la mise en service à travers les projets.
Assurer la rétroaction et la résolution des enjeux de qualité identifiés durant la mise en service avec les fournisseurs, les partenaires et les équipes d’ingénierie.
Développer des partenariats avec des établissements d’enseignement afin de créer un bassin de talents pour soutenir les projets futurs et la croissance de l’entreprise.
Mettre en place et animer une gouvernance de résolution de problèmes afin de garantir que les enjeux soient traités à leur cause fondamentale.
Développer les gestionnaires et chefs d’équipe et instaurer une culture axée sur la responsabilisation, la sécurité et la rapidité d’exécution.

Approvisionnement

Développer et maintenir des relations solides avec les fournisseurs actuels.
Gérer la base de données des fournisseurs ainsi que leur qualification commerciale.
Gérer les contrats, les bons de commande et les ententes-cadres avec les fournisseurs.
Assurer le suivi des commandes et sécuriser les dates de livraison.
Organiser des revues trimestrielles avec les fournisseurs, en collaboration avec les équipes d’approvisionnement et de programme.

Qualité fournisseurs

Réaliser les audits fournisseurs et les processus d’intégration (onboarding).
Exécuter les FAT (Factory Acceptance Tests), inspections et essais selon les plans d’inspection et d’essais (ITP) établis par l’ingénierie.
Gérer les non-conformités (NCR), les analyses de causes fondamentales et les actions correctives fournisseurs afin que chaque commande soit meilleure que la précédente.
Maintenir les tableaux de performance des fournisseurs et gérer les réclamations sous garantie.

Logistique et transport

Planifier, exécuter et assurer le suivi des opérations de transport de marchandises à l’échelle mondiale.
Gérer les douanes et les importations au Canada et aux États-Unis ainsi que les contrats avec les transporteurs et transitaires.
Superviser la réception, l’entreposage et la livraison sur site, incluant la gestion des dommages et des réclamations.

Mise en service (Commissioning)

Être responsable du plan et du calendrier de mise en service ainsi que de la gestion des activités sur site.
Diriger les activités de pré-mise en service, les inspections préalables (walkdowns) ainsi que les essais de niveaux L1 à L3 avec le client et les fonctions de soutien.
Clôturer les listes de déficiences (RFI) et gérer la remise finale au client ainsi que la clôture du projet.

Jalons de projet (Stage Gates)

Superviser les aspects opérationnels des jalons du projet :
Libération majeure des achats (G4)
Autorisation du chantier (G6)
Complétion mécanique (G7)
Premier démarrage ou mise sous tension (G8)
Remise finale au client (G9)

Budget et performance commerciale

Gérer le budget des opérations ainsi que les dépenses liées aux achats, à la mise en service et au transport.
Soutenir les activités d’approvisionnement lors de la négociation des contrats fournisseurs, des ententes-cadres et des tarifs logistiques.
Récupérer les coûts liés aux défauts fournisseurs et aux retards de livraison au moyen de rétrofacturations (back-charges) et de réclamations sous garantie.

Rapports et gestion des escalades

Présenter mensuellement à la direction exécutive les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) relatifs à la livraison, à la qualité, à la mise en service et aux coûts.
Fournir un rapport hebdomadaire sur l’ensemble des activités en cours et mettre en évidence les risques et les opportunités.
Escalader rapidement les risques d’approvisionnement en présentant un plan d’atténuation et un responsable clairement identifié.

Ce que vous apportez à l’organisation

Exigences

Baccalauréat en génie, en gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ou en gestion des opérations.
Plus de 12 ans d’expérience en opérations, en chaîne d’approvisionnement ou en livraison de projets liés à des équipements électriques lourds, mécaniques ou de production d’énergie, dont au moins 5 ans à la tête d’organisations regroupant plusieurs équipes.
Expérience pratique dans les centres de données ou autres installations critiques : génératrices, refroidisseurs (chillers), appareillage électrique (switchgear), UPS (alimentations sans interruption) ou turbines à gaz.
Expérience démontrée en développement de fournisseurs, négociation contractuelle et gestion de la qualité fournisseurs (FAT, ITP, NCR et actions correctives).
Expérience dans la gestion du transport international, des charges hors normes et des formalités douanières au Canada et aux États-Unis.
Connaissance des niveaux de mise en service L1 à L3 et des pratiques de transfert de projet.
Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais; le français constitue un atout important pour le poste basé à Montréal.

Atouts

Titre d’ingénieur (P.Eng.) ou admissibilité à l’obtention du titre.
Certification PMP.
Certification APICS/ASCM (CPIM ou CSCP).
Expérience dans la mise en place d’une organisation des opérations ou de la chaîne d’approvisionnement à partir de zéro.
Expérience au sein d’un fabricant d’équipement d’origine (OEM) ou d’un entrepreneur EPC desservant des exploitants hyperscale ou de colocation.

Le rendement sera évalué selon un ensemble d’indicateurs de performance (KPI) propres à chacune des équipes. Les objectifs seront établis conjointement avec la direction après les 90 premiers jours en poste.

Ce poste est offert dans un environnement de travail hybride nécessitant une présence régulière au bureau :
Présence obligatoire au bureau trois (3) jours par semaine
.
Les lundis et vendredis
sont des journées obligatoires de présence au bureau.

Pourquoi vous joindre à nous?

Équipe dynamique et expérimentée bénéficiant d’un club social actif.
Horaire flexible et environnement de travail hybride.
Régime d’avantages sociaux et dentaires généreux.
Minimum de quatre (4) semaines de vacances.
Occasion unique de bâtir, développer et faire croître une organisation en pleine expansion.

Qui sommes-nous?

Fondé en 2020, le Groupe Adag
répond à la demande croissante pour les centres de données et les infrastructures critiques, stimulée par l'essor du télétravail, des services infonuagiques et de l'intelligence artificielle. Forts d'une présence au Canada et aux États-Unis, nous offrons une gamme complète de services spécialisés en centres de données dans ces régions.

De la gestion de projet à la conception, en passant par la modélisation CFD et l'approvisionnement, nous intégrons des pratiques durables à chacune de nos solutions afin d'aider nos clients à répondre à leurs besoins opérationnels tout en réduisant leur impact environnemental.

Chez le Groupe Adag, nous sommes fiers de notre agilité, qui nous permet de réaliser des projets dans des délais serrés tout en maintenant les plus hauts standards de qualité. Nous nous engageons à façonner l'avenir des solutions de centres de données en plaçant la durabilité au cœur de notre approche. Joignez-vous à nous et construisons l'avenir ensemble!

Chez Adag, nous favorisons un milieu de travail inclusif où chaque personne a l'occasion de s'épanouir et d'atteindre son plein potentiel. Nous vous encourageons à être vous-même au travail. Nous accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées et serons heureux d'évaluer votre profil dans le cadre de notre processus de recrutement. Nous vous remercions de votre intérêt envers Adag. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role:

Elastic Security is hiring a Senior Director of Product Management to lead our Endpoint Security & XDR business. This role reports to the GM of Elastic Security. You will be paired with our most senior engineering leader, a VP who leads all of Elastic Security engineering and whose day-to-day focus is endpoint, sharing accountability for the line's outcomes with you. You will also peer with the product lead of our SIEM and analytics business as we build one platform together. The endpoint is where we meet the adversary directly, and where the people we serve, the analysts and defenders protecting hospitals, banks, and government networks, need us most. Their mission is our mission, and this role carries that responsibility for the endpoint and XDR market. Like Elastic itself, the role is distributed by design.

This business was born when Elastic acquired Endgame in 2019, a pioneer in endpoint prevention, detection, and response with roots in defending national security networks. We extended that protection philosophy to Linux and cloud-native environments with the Cmd acquisition in 2021. The result today is Elastic Defend, and its record in independent testing reflects the quality of the work: Elastic Security was the only vendor to score 100% protection in both the AV-Comparatives Real-World and Malware Protection Tests for all of 2025, and the only vendor among 16 to earn a perfect malware protection score in the 2026 Business Security Test, with zero false alarms on the software businesses actually run. And unlike most of this market, we do that work in the open: our protection artifacts and detection rules are public for anyone to inspect.

This role is open for a straightforward reason. Our product leader is retiring, and we are organizing product management around our two core businesses: SIEM and analytics, which will be led by a proven leader already at Elastic, and endpoint, where we are looking outside for someone who brings a fresh perspective from this market. The timing is deliberate in another way as well: security operations are shifting toward agentic workflows, and as a challenger in this market we can move faster than the incumbents. Our focus with this role is business expertise: we are looking for a business owner who understands endpoint security deeply and who will grow this line with the care of someone who owns the outcome. You will have genuine room to lead. The strategy, the priorities, and how we compete are yours to shape with your engineering partner.

What You Will Be Doing:

Drive the business-driven OKRs for the Endpoint Security & XDR line: revenue contribution, competitive win rate, platform attach, retention, and expansion.
Set the product strategy for the line and represent it with sales leadership, customers, and analysts: a clear diagnosis of the market, a guiding policy, and coherent actions that follow from it.
Own the agentic detection and response strategy for the endpoint: where AI-driven and autonomous capabilities genuinely help prevention, detection, and response at the edge, working closely with the SIEM and analytics line so customers experience one agentic platform, not two roadmaps.
Shape where we invest and where we choose not to, building the case with data and customer evidence.
Own how endpoint and XDR fit the broader Elastic Security platform story, so a customer who lands with endpoint expands into the platform and a SIEM customer sees why our endpoint belongs next to it.
Put customers first. Visit them where they are, participate in deals and win/loss reviews, enable the field, and represent Elastic at tradeshows and industry events. This work requires regular travel.
Partner with your engineering counterpart as a true pair, sharing one set of outcomes for the line.
Lead and develop a team of product managers, helping each of them connect their work to the customer's mission and the business.

What You Bring:

Genuine care for the people this product protects. Customers can tell whether the person across the table is invested in their mission, and this business runs on the trust you earn by caring consistently over time.
Business expertise running a product line or business unit in security, with comfort in the full picture: revenue, win rates, retention, pricing and packaging, and competitive positioning.
Earned credibility in endpoint security: EPP, EDR, XDR, and enough understanding of what an agent does on a machine to have real conversations with engineers and practitioners.
A strong working partnership with go-to-market teams, including experience enabling sellers and supporting deals alongside the field.
A habit of deciding with evidence: win/loss data, customer conversations, and market signals inform your calls.
A point of view on how a challenger competes and differentiates against well-funded incumbents.
Clear executive communication with executive leadership, CISOs, sales leadership, and industry analysts.

Bonus Points:

Experience competing with or working at endpoint-focused security vendors, with perspective on the strengths and gaps across the market.
Experience helping a security business scale from a few hundred million toward $1B.
Familiarity with public efficacy testing (AV-Comparatives, MITRE ATT&CK evaluations) and how to participate in the open.
Experience serving customers in hard environments: regulated industries, classified networks, air-gapped and OT deployments.
A thoughtful position on AI and agentic capabilities at the endpoint, with healthy skepticism of silver bullets and a clear sense of where they genuinely help the defender.
Contributions to open source or the security community. Our work is public, and we value people who build in the open.

Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People:

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.

Build, lead, and develop FinDev Canada's Climate Mobilization Team.
Lead the execution and evolution of FinDev Canada's Climate Mobilization Strategy and climate opportunity pipeline.

Shape opportunities from early-stage concepts through investment readiness.

Strengthen FinDev Canada's institutional capabilities and thought leadership in climate mobilisation.

*

While this job posting may display only a limited number of locations, we welcome applications from qualified candidates globally. If you believe your skills and experience match this role, we encourage you to apply regardless of your current location.

. The selected candidate will be employed and hosted through their current ABB location or the nearest suitable ABB office

Establish customer confidence early. Engage owners, EPCs and licensors as ABB’s execution lead, building trusted relationships with project directors, engineering managers, procurement teams and executive stakeholders.
Make delivery experience a competitive advantage. Present credible reference cases that explain project scope, outcomes, challenges, recovery actions and lessons learned.

Preserve continuity after award. Ensure a structured handover of commitments, assumptions, risks and customer expectations. Where assigned, lead execution as Project Director or remain involved as executive sponsor through critical phases.
Strengthen ABB’s pursuit and delivery capability. Collaborate across Sales, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Legal and Finance; coach teams; and feed execution outcomes into future estimates, reference cases and delivery practices.

Your background

A degree in instrumentation, control, electrical, chemical engineering or an equivalent discipline; an executive or business master’s degree is an advantage.
At least 12 years of industrial automation project delivery experience, including substantial responsibility as Project Manager or Project Director on large, complex projects in oil and gas, chemicals, refining or energy.
Full-lifecycle leadership of at least one extra-large or highly complex automation project, together with direct experience recovering a challenged project.
Demonstrated contribution to winning major pursuits, such as MAC selections, FEED-to-EPC conversions or frame agreements.
Deep understanding of EPC delivery, contracting models, interface management and the dynamics between owners, EPCs and technology vendors.
Working knowledge of DCS, SIS, PLC/SCADA, advanced process control and OT/IT convergence, enabling you to connect execution choices with customers’ operational outcomes.

You build trust through first-hand delivery experience, candid advice and confidence with customer executives and EPC leaders. You connect execution decisions with commercial value and unite Sales and delivery teams around realistic, shared commitments.

Engage customers earlier, strengthen ABB’s execution credibility and help win strategic projects - supported by smooth handovers, protected margins and lessons that improve future pursuits.

The final offer will be tailored based on your role location, experience, skills and qualifications, internal market positioning and alignment with ABB internal standards.

Directeur(trice) des opérations

Le poste

Eco DCS, une entreprise du Groupe Adag située à Montréal, fournit des infrastructures complètes d’alimentation électrique et de refroidissement pour les centres de données : génératrices diesel, refroidisseurs (chillers), murs de ventilateurs (fan walls), turbines à gaz, appareillage de commutation moyenne tension (MV switchgear) et unités de contrôle électrique.

Le ou la Directeur(trice) des opérations
est responsable de quatre équipes de bout en bout (Approvisionnement, Qualité fournisseurs, Logistique et transport, Mise en service) et veille à ce que tout défaut soit retracé jusqu’au fournisseur et corrigé de façon permanente. Notre philosophie est simple : « Livré. » Offrir des centres de données fiables dans des délais de réalisation réduits.

Portée du rôle
: Les Opérations sont responsables de l’exécution et de la livraison. L’Ingénierie conserve l’autorité technique quant aux exigences, aux critères FAT et ITP, à la disposition des NCR ainsi qu’à la décision finale de mise en service.

Gestionnaires relevant directement du poste :

Gestionnaire Approvisionnement
Gestionnaire Qualité fournisseurs
Gestionnaire Logistique et transport
Directeur(trice) de la mise en service

Rôle, responsabilités et objectifs

Construire la fonction Opérations

Concevoir, recruter et diriger les quatre équipes Opérations, incluant les agents d’approvisionnement, les gestionnaires de la qualité de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, les coordonnateurs logistiques et l’équipe de mise en service.
Collaborer avec les équipes de programme afin d’assurer que l’exécution des projets respecte les meilleures pratiques et les standards de référence.
Rédiger et faire appliquer les procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP) pour l’approvisionnement, le suivi des commandes, l’expédition, la réception, l’inspection et la mise en service.
Mettre en place des outils permettant le suivi des commandes, des expéditions, des non-conformités (NCR) et de l’état d’avancement de la mise en service à travers les projets.
Assurer la rétroaction et la résolution des enjeux de qualité identifiés durant la mise en service avec les fournisseurs, les partenaires et les équipes d’ingénierie.
Développer des partenariats avec des établissements d’enseignement afin de créer un bassin de talents pour soutenir les projets futurs et la croissance de l’entreprise.
Mettre en place et animer une gouvernance de résolution de problèmes afin de garantir que les enjeux soient traités à leur cause fondamentale.
Développer les gestionnaires et chefs d’équipe et instaurer une culture axée sur la responsabilisation, la sécurité et la rapidité d’exécution.

Approvisionnement

Développer et maintenir des relations solides avec les fournisseurs actuels.
Gérer la base de données des fournisseurs ainsi que leur qualification commerciale.
Gérer les contrats, les bons de commande et les ententes-cadres avec les fournisseurs.
Assurer le suivi des commandes et sécuriser les dates de livraison.
Organiser des revues trimestrielles avec les fournisseurs, en collaboration avec les équipes d’approvisionnement et de programme.

Qualité fournisseurs

Réaliser les audits fournisseurs et les processus d’intégration (onboarding).
Exécuter les FAT (Factory Acceptance Tests), inspections et essais selon les plans d’inspection et d’essais (ITP) établis par l’ingénierie.
Gérer les non-conformités (NCR), les analyses de causes fondamentales et les actions correctives fournisseurs afin que chaque commande soit meilleure que la précédente.
Maintenir les tableaux de performance des fournisseurs et gérer les réclamations sous garantie.

Logistique et transport

Planifier, exécuter et assurer le suivi des opérations de transport de marchandises à l’échelle mondiale.
Gérer les douanes et les importations au Canada et aux États-Unis ainsi que les contrats avec les transporteurs et transitaires.
Superviser la réception, l’entreposage et la livraison sur site, incluant la gestion des dommages et des réclamations.

Mise en service (Commissioning)

Être responsable du plan et du calendrier de mise en service ainsi que de la gestion des activités sur site.
Diriger les activités de pré-mise en service, les inspections préalables (walkdowns) ainsi que les essais de niveaux L1 à L3 avec le client et les fonctions de soutien.
Clôturer les listes de déficiences (RFI) et gérer la remise finale au client ainsi que la clôture du projet.

Jalons de projet (Stage Gates)

Superviser les aspects opérationnels des jalons du projet :
Libération majeure des achats (G4)
Autorisation du chantier (G6)
Complétion mécanique (G7)
Premier démarrage ou mise sous tension (G8)
Remise finale au client (G9)

Budget et performance commerciale

Gérer le budget des opérations ainsi que les dépenses liées aux achats, à la mise en service et au transport.
Soutenir les activités d’approvisionnement lors de la négociation des contrats fournisseurs, des ententes-cadres et des tarifs logistiques.
Récupérer les coûts liés aux défauts fournisseurs et aux retards de livraison au moyen de rétrofacturations (back-charges) et de réclamations sous garantie.

Rapports et gestion des escalades

Présenter mensuellement à la direction exécutive les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) relatifs à la livraison, à la qualité, à la mise en service et aux coûts.
Fournir un rapport hebdomadaire sur l’ensemble des activités en cours et mettre en évidence les risques et les opportunités.
Escalader rapidement les risques d’approvisionnement en présentant un plan d’atténuation et un responsable clairement identifié.

Ce que vous apportez à l’organisation

Exigences

Baccalauréat en génie, en gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ou en gestion des opérations.
Plus de 12 ans d’expérience en opérations, en chaîne d’approvisionnement ou en livraison de projets liés à des équipements électriques lourds, mécaniques ou de production d’énergie, dont au moins 5 ans à la tête d’organisations regroupant plusieurs équipes.
Expérience pratique dans les centres de données ou autres installations critiques : génératrices, refroidisseurs (chillers), appareillage électrique (switchgear), UPS (alimentations sans interruption) ou turbines à gaz.
Expérience démontrée en développement de fournisseurs, négociation contractuelle et gestion de la qualité fournisseurs (FAT, ITP, NCR et actions correctives).
Expérience dans la gestion du transport international, des charges hors normes et des formalités douanières au Canada et aux États-Unis.
Connaissance des niveaux de mise en service L1 à L3 et des pratiques de transfert de projet.
Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais; le français constitue un atout important pour le poste basé à Montréal.

Atouts

Titre d’ingénieur (P.Eng.) ou admissibilité à l’obtention du titre.
Certification PMP.
Certification APICS/ASCM (CPIM ou CSCP).
Expérience dans la mise en place d’une organisation des opérations ou de la chaîne d’approvisionnement à partir de zéro.
Expérience au sein d’un fabricant d’équipement d’origine (OEM) ou d’un entrepreneur EPC desservant des exploitants hyperscale ou de colocation.

Le rendement sera évalué selon un ensemble d’indicateurs de performance (KPI) propres à chacune des équipes. Les objectifs seront établis conjointement avec la direction après les 90 premiers jours en poste.

Ce poste est offert dans un environnement de travail hybride nécessitant une présence régulière au bureau :
Présence obligatoire au bureau trois (3) jours par semaine
.
Les lundis et vendredis
sont des journées obligatoires de présence au bureau.

Pourquoi vous joindre à nous?

Équipe dynamique et expérimentée bénéficiant d’un club social actif.
Horaire flexible et environnement de travail hybride.
Régime d’avantages sociaux et dentaires généreux.
Minimum de quatre (4) semaines de vacances.
Occasion unique de bâtir, développer et faire croître une organisation en pleine expansion.

Qui sommes-nous?

Fondé en 2020, le Groupe Adag
répond à la demande croissante pour les centres de données et les infrastructures critiques, stimulée par l'essor du télétravail, des services infonuagiques et de l'intelligence artificielle. Forts d'une présence au Canada et aux États-Unis, nous offrons une gamme complète de services spécialisés en centres de données dans ces régions.

De la gestion de projet à la conception, en passant par la modélisation CFD et l'approvisionnement, nous intégrons des pratiques durables à chacune de nos solutions afin d'aider nos clients à répondre à leurs besoins opérationnels tout en réduisant leur impact environnemental.

Chez le Groupe Adag, nous sommes fiers de notre agilité, qui nous permet de réaliser des projets dans des délais serrés tout en maintenant les plus hauts standards de qualité. Nous nous engageons à façonner l'avenir des solutions de centres de données en plaçant la durabilité au cœur de notre approche. Joignez-vous à nous et construisons l'avenir ensemble!

Chez Adag, nous favorisons un milieu de travail inclusif où chaque personne a l'occasion de s'épanouir et d'atteindre son plein potentiel. Nous vous encourageons à être vous-même au travail. Nous accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées et serons heureux d'évaluer votre profil dans le cadre de notre processus de recrutement. Nous vous remercions de votre intérêt envers Adag. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées.

Head of Operations
